_about: Every genre's numbers for Jam, in one place: the engine reads this file (crates/engine/src/jam.rs) and so does the known-answer generator (tests/fixtures/gen_p36_expected.py). To tune a genre: change a number here, run scripts/python.sh -I tests/fixtures/gen_p36_expected.py --write tests/fixtures, look at what moved in p36_expected.json, then run scripts/check.sh. A hit: step 0 to 15, half (half a step later), length in steps (chords, bass), pitch (bass only: root, fifth, octave_up, octave_down, next_degree), chance or unless in per cent (neither: always), and base (a velocity in hundredths, less the part's jitter) or exact (no jitter). A part: hits, either (one chance a bar picks then or otherwise) or last_bar, with jitter (how far below its base a velocity may fall, 16 hundredths unless given). Each voice, the chords, the bass and the melody are lists of variants: a roll draws one of each (none when there is one), and a variant's _note says in plain words how it goes. A drum, chord or bass variant is a list of parts, drawn in order; a melody variant has its own count, starts and late chance, the band its notes walk in (low and high keys, an octave or more apart) and the most steps a note lasts (max_length).
